elements.text: The Need for a European Policy
EU Food law developed incrementally over a long period of time.
Treaty of Rome made no explicit mention of consumer protection or public health.
Not until the Single European Act 1986 and Maastricht Treaty of 1992 were consumer protection and public health introduced as goals.
Food Law concentrated on the free movement of foodstuffs in the earlier years.
1962: The first EU food Directive — concerned with colours in foodstuffs
1979: Cassis de Dijon and other cases — pushed EU to reorientate its food law
